scope: D187 duplicate-rename native harness routing, observation and cleanup; no product or hosted-browser acceptance claim.

evidence.inventory: EXT-F-1007-T04 and T29 remain partial. The reviewed Project receipt 38030536461 and no-destination receipt 38044665604 establish adjacent member substeps; both leave duplicate and refusal/retry unverified.
evidence.routing: Workflow and runner admit duplicate-rename only for scrape-save-member with member auth and destination none. Default single mode remains the existing route; other cases and destinations reject duplicate scope.
evidence.duplicate_flow: The native driver saves a custom-named Source, independently reads its row and zero edges, recaptures the same run-owned article, and submits a second custom name without a destination. The observer requires one successful /sources/land response with reused_existing=true and the original Source ID, plus one successful POST to /sources/<original-id>/edit. Independent readback requires exactly one active row with the renamed value and same ID, no edges, then reopens and checks the renamed Source and captured content.
evidence.cleanup: Cleanup is constrained to valid IDs matching the run-unique canonical identity, selected organization and extension origin. Duplicate mode allows at most two rows; each matching row has edges removed and is soft-deleted with exact identity predicates, then active rows and edges are read back. Ambiguous counts fail before broad deletion.
evidence.report_privacy: Native report records auth booleans and organization resolution, not credentials, email, tokens, request bodies or response text. Duplicate observer returns booleans only; failure output is reduced to a constrained code.
evidence.saved_and_refusal: Saved is derived from the current capture and organization state and has no timer in ScrapeView, so the post-response check is not a short-lived toast check. The run does not measure confirmation latency. Controlled refusal, retry and rename recovery are outside this scope.
